cards.front: How to name a metric in an interview
cards.back: Name the metric, give one target number, and say how you would measure it.
Time from a source change to it being searchable. Example target: p95 under 15 minutes.
Share of questions where a relevant chunk is in the top k. Example target: recall@5 of at least 0.85.
MRR measures how high the first relevant result ranks (1 means always first). NDCG@k rewards the most relevant items sitting near the top.
Share of answer claims supported by the retrieved sources. Example target: at least 95%.
The text-to-SQL metric: the query's result matches the expected result. Example target: at least 85%.
Task success checks the end state in a sandbox, not just the text (≥ 85%). Argument accuracy checks ids, amounts and dates are exactly right (≥ 98%).
Agents are not deterministic, so run each case 3 to 5 times and report the rate, not one run.
A 0.8 score is right about 80% of the time. Check it before using scores as confidence.
Benign questions wrongly refused. Example target: 3% or less.
Inter-rater kappa of at least 0.7, and judge-human agreement of at least 80% before an LLM judge gates releases.
Compare every metric with the current version per slice: no slice may drop more than 1 point.

quiz.q: You need ±3 points of precision on a measured rate per slice. About how many examples per slice?
quiz.why: The confidence interval shrinks with more examples; ±3 points needs about 400 per slice.

quiz.q: Which belongs as a guardrail in an A/B test, not the primary metric?
choices: The one business metric decided up front
quiz.why: Run one primary metric, with CSAT, latency, cost and safety as guardrails that must not get worse.

quiz.q: What should check citation accuracy: an LLM judge or code?
choices: Code: every cited id exists, was retrieved and supports the claim
quiz.why: Use code for anything exact, and judges only for fuzzy qualities.

quiz.q: Positives are rare. Which curve compares models better?
quiz.why: PR-AUC is better than ROC-AUC when positives are rare.

quiz.q: A canary at 5% shows thumbs-down up 40%. What should happen?
quiz.why: Canary guardrails auto-roll back if errors double or thumbs-down rises 30%.

quiz.q: Users are editing drafts more often than last month. What does that signal?
quiz.why: Rising edit rate on drafts is a production sign that quality dropped.

quiz.q: Which safety metric is a release blocker at zero?
quiz.why: Any answer revealing data the user cannot see blocks the release.
